rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a material immigration-veto template. Both memoranda describe an alien admitted temporarily, explain that a private bill would confer permanent-resident status, insist that the conditions of temporary admission should be honored absent exceptional facts, and warn that special relief would encourage other aliens to use temporary admission as a route around ordinary immigration requirements. C12 and C08 share the more general private-bill framework of rejecting individualized exceptions to uniform statutory rules, but their veterans-benefit contexts and less specific language make them weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Mr. Mnatzakanian... entered the United States in 1951 as an exchange student... The bill would grant permanent residence immigration status to the beneficiaries.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This alien entered the United States as a visitor... The bill would grant her the status of a lawful permanent resident
shared_material.explanation: Both establish temporary admission followed by a private bill seeking permanent-resident status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: we can maintain our exchange programs... only if both the participants and the United States observe the conditions of the exchange... Except in such cases, the return rule is necessary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: she should be required to depart in accordance with the terms under which she was granted admission to this country
shared_material.explanation: Both make compliance with the conditions of temporary admission the central operative principle.

shared_material.child_excerpt: other aliens are encouraged to use the exchange program as an avenue to immigration
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The enactment of this bill undoubtedly would encourage other aliens to attempt to enter the United States as visitors for a temporary period and thereafter seek exemption from requirements of the immigration laws through special legislation.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared policy warning that individualized relief would induce misuse of temporary-entry programs as immigration channels.
